drafted_from: tool:tell-our-own-voice-from-what-was-heard's own row (its words, input schema and sample run) and what that sample answered when do-work/check-heard-echo.mjs ran it here
start_here: Say to your AI: "Check whether the words just heard, \"The recording finished and the transcript is ready\", were our own spoken notice from one second earlier." It runs tool:tell-our-own-voice-from-what-was-heard with the notices the account kept and answers which notice the words echo.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it reads the echo settings and notification rows you give it (or your content-setting records) and writes nothing.
instructions: 1. Gather the notices the account spoke recently (kind, seq, at, title, body), the heard text and the time it was heard.
2. Give the echo settings and notification rows in the input, or keep them as record:content-setting:heard-echo and record:content-setting:tell-the-person so the tool reads them.
3. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:tell-our-own-voice-from-what-was-heard and that input.
4. Read echo: a notice and its evidence means the words were our own voice, so do not treat them as a request; null means a person said them.

worked_examples.title: A spoken notice heard back one second later is named as our own voice
worked_examples.ask: Were the words just heard our own notice being read out?

notices.body: The recording finished and the transcript is ready
